title: Sharbel Makhlouf (24 July)
hookLine: a Maronite hermit of Lebanon, who kept silence for years

cards: High in the mountains of Lebanon, above a monastery, there's a small stone hermitage. One monk lives there. He rises in the dark to pray.
He works the vineyard with his hands. He eats once a day, tradition says, and very little. He speaks only when he must.
He wrote no books that we know of, and gave no well-known sermons. And yet today pilgrims crowd the road to that mountain. Today, a saint whose teaching was silence.

teach.h: A MONK OF THE MARONITE CHURCH.
teach.b: Sharbel Makhlouf was a monk of the Maronite Church.

The Maronites are Eastern Catholics, rooted in Lebanon, in full communion with the pope, with their own ancient liturgy, prayed in part in Syriac, a form of Aramaic, close to the language Jesus spoke.
So he's a Catholic saint from a branch of the Catholic family some listeners may not know. He was born with another name and took the name Sharbel when he became a monk.

teach.h: HE ASKED TO LIVE AS A HERMIT.
teach.b: After years in the monastery, he asked to live as a hermit, and he spent the rest of his life in that hermitage, in prayer and silence, for many years, tradition says. Why silence?
In the books of Kings, Elijah waits on a mountain for God. A great wind passes, then an earthquake, then fire, and the Lord is not in them.

teach.h: GOD IN THE QUIET AFTER THE FIRE.
teach.b: Then, in the Douay-Rheims: "after the fire a whistling of a gentle air." Not in the noise.
In the quiet after it. Stories gathered around him even while he lived. Tradition tells of a lamp the other monks filled with water as a test, and it burned anyway.
After his death the stories multiplied, of light seen at his grave, of healings, and pilgrims began to come, and still do.

teach.h: A WHISTLING OF A GENTLE AIR.
teach.b: The Church examined these claims before naming him a saint. But the heart of it is simple. A man went quiet for God, for years, and that quiet still draws people up a mountain.

how: Maronite Catholics and others honor Saint Sharbel, and pilgrims visit his monastery and hermitage in the mountains of Lebanon to pray.

games.q: you're a monk in a busy monastery, close to God and to your brothers. something pulls you further. what do you ask for?
o: to live alone as a hermit.
games.why: Sharbel asked to live as a hermit, and spent the rest of his life in prayer and silence in the hermitage.

practice: For these minutes, no words, not even in your head if you can help it; when a sentence starts, let it trail off. Hear what's left: the room, the street, your breath.
If you pray, rest in that gentle air from Elijah's mountain; if you don't, let the quiet be enough.

wordCard.voice: Sharbel Makhlouf. A Maronite monk of Lebanon who lived his last years as a hermit, in prayer and silence.
